The game has issues but it is VERY fun despite the problems.  The devs are also working on a total recode to fix the current issues and expand the game with more of everything.
Playing as a dino in third person view is exciting and rewarding.  Working in small packs hunting humans is very enjoyable.  Stalking a good human player and finally taking them out is a real rush.
Playing as a human in first person view is also a great deal of fun.  Playing as a human you feel weak and vulnerable so your level of paranoia is always high.  Stick with other players and work as a team to defend and take down the fast and powerful dinos.
Every class is very playable and has its own advantages and disadvantages making the game a different experience for each class.  Some are utility classes, some are damage dealing but all can be lethal.  It shouldn't be difficult to find a class to suit your preferred play style.

Wizards aren’t very agile creatures, so making them the main characters in an FPS might seems like a strange choice. You won’t be sprinting across the battlefield, you can’t even crouch due to your elderly wizard knees. Your only weapon will be your bare hands and the element of your choice. Destroy your foes with fire, lightning, or even the power of the nether. Currently there are 6 classes, each offering their own unique playstyle. While some class roles are fairly obvious, like nature wizards having the ability to heal, the actual execution is entirely up to you. Tweaking your playstyle is made even easier by allowing you to pick your own “utility” and “mobility” spells. Feel like blasting your enemies from a rooftop? Use a mobility teleport to get on the roof and rain destruction down. Playing a long-range class, but not great at aiming? Use a utility binding spell to keep your enemies still for a second. The action is fast-paced and based on completely on skill. It’s early access, but the potential is there. Here it comes, Grimoire- Manastorm!
The spell effects are pretty great, especially viewed from third-person. In first person some of them are a bit lackluster, but that is to be expected during early access. The character models look nice, as do the levels. There are control point and team deathmatch game modes available. It’s a pretty awesome feeling, watching two teams of wizards slinging spells at each other. Spells move at different speeds, but most are able to be dodged with some quick reflexes. You are able to use a blink called “mana-step” to traverse ground quickly. Mana-step is the only skill that seems to use mana, which means you can sling all the spells you please. Not worrying about mana makes the combat much more frantic, as neither wizard will generally ever stop casting during combat. Blinking behind a cart to dodge an icebolt and returning fire with your own spell school is intense, and with a full server the action is constant.
There doesn’t seem to be any damage multipliers based on elemental strengths and weaknesses, a la Pokemon, but I think it would be a nice addition to strengthen the class-based gameplay. The classes seem to still require some tweaking and balancing. My roommate and I both found ice to be extremely overpowering to almost any other class. Ice is a relatively close-range class, so picking lightning and striking from afar seems to castrate your opponent relatively well. Aiming better than your opponent is really less than half of the battle. Knowing which spells your opponents are likely to use, and how to counter them is what will end up winning wars. Thinking on your feet, and using wits along with clever use of spells is exactly what being a mage is all about, and to see it come to life in such a fantastic way is something to behold. However, it is still early access, so there are a couple of blemishes.
The biggest obstacle the game will need to overcome is a loyal player-base. There are dev playtests 3 times weekly, which makes it relatively easy to get the full experience but in off-hours most matches you find will be 1v1. I would like to see a free-for-all deathmatch mode, since the occasional 2v1 isn’t really a fun experience. There is also currently no music aside from the main menu, though that music is quite epic and mythical. I would also like to see a bit more variety in the levels, and to have the first-person spell effects be kicked up a notch. There is time for all of the above to be fully fleshed out, and if you can find a decent match, what is offered is amazingly fun. I suggest it to anyone who enjoys a real time battle of wits and reflexes whilst slinging a bevy of spells at your opponent. Thanks to Omniconnection for the review copy. Here’s to hoping Grimoire- Manastorm will blossom into what it deserves to be.

Basically, Bunnylord needs you to kill every single mob boss and their gang members so that he can be voted as mayor of whatever city he lives in, so that he can then save the world. Throughout the cutscenes before and after each day, a couple of random word generators are thrown in. So maybe you select a mission and it's "Arrow hat day", and you replay it and now it's "hostage day" just to add some silliness to the game.
The fighting in this game, is simple yet super satisfying. X to roll or take cover, C to shoot, and V for grenades/special attack. It fits great with the 2 1/4 dimensions of the game, and with the amount of cover that you have, you shouldn't ever be left very vulnerable. The enemies are like any other shooter, you have the ones with shotguns, pistols, smgs, and the like.
There are 9 characters to choose from that you can unlock as the game progresses each character is fairly different from the others, though there are some that share similar abilities. (Such as Samantha and Clide, both can run n gun) . My personal favorites are Kimmy and Clive
Side missions are fun, every mission has 3 optional missions for you to complete, and each one you do gets you a better rank (0=Mayor, 1=Prime Minister, 2=King of England, 3=Global Megalord) And you get different endings depending on your rank at the end of the game.
Again, I absolutley love this game, and cannot express how much I want a sequel, or at least a level editor.

Bioshock 2 pretty much starts you off a powerhouse. What can I say about this game? It's truly amazing in just about every way, and i've only been playing ~10 hours at the time of writing this review. I will go through a big wall of text explaining what I love about this, but for you folks short on time i'll include a pros and cons sorta TLDR below.
First off, the visuals. Right from the get-go, im struck with near cuphead levels of hand drawn lively characters, beautiful enemy designs, intimidating bosses, everything you can love about a game visually is packed into this little masterpiece. If youre a fan of somber and melancholy, yet beautiful scenes (especially with rain (like me)), this game is packed to the brim with it. Even aside from the somber side of things, there are lively characters tucked away under all the sorrow and death; ones who even after exploring through these ruins are still chipper and friendly. Many of these can be found above ground after your initial meeting, then later on in the ruins, all of them living their own lives with you just finding them from time to time somewhat like NPCs in dark souls. There is also an overwhelming diversity in these locations, ranging from a dead and decrepit crossroads, to the lush green landscapes of the greenpath, to the forgotten structures that populate the rain-filled, beautiful atmosphere of the City of Tears.
Next, the music and sfx in this game. The music is simply PHENOMENAL, and is quite reminiscent of pikmin at times, notably the greenpath's theme. This area's music is a wonderful example of how atmospheric this game can be, as it pulls you right out of the otherwise somber world this game presents, with a sense of life and adventure you seldom find elsewhere. It still has the violin reminding you of how this used to be a beautiful part of the insect's cities, but the other instruments all overwhelmingly show how one kind of beauty can reclaim others, both working together to make something truly unique. the sense of vitality this presents works wonderfully with the aggressive landscape, reminding you that at every turn the fauna and flora here are against you. It is also where you meet the hunter, who I will touch on later. Lastly the boss's themes in this are a wonderful change of pace as (for example) the protagonist draws it's nail, and suddenly in something that is aggressive enough to be in a bullet hell, harpsichords begin striking as a mantis lord flies from its throne and begins darting around the field.
Next, I will go over some of the NPCs. Most you can get a grasp of their personality before you even see them, as many sing, munch, or hum to pass the time as they go through their own adventures alone most of the time. You walk into their room, and from across the screen they are already moving and goimng about their own duties, whether they are mining, making a map, selling things to those who pass by, or just eating some tasty mushroom they found in an abandoned stagway. Speaking of which even the fast travel medium is an npc with a voice, movement, and stories to tell! There's also the hunter who I mentioned earlier. He is a giant insect hiding in brush with glowing red eyes, hidden behind huge teethlike rocks guarding the entrance to his room. When you enter he seems like a boss or huge enemy, yet when you talk to him he is somewhat friendly towards you for being so brave, and even gives you his journal which gives flavor text for enemies you encounter. It's just an interesting presentation for an NPC that I don't often see. I'm probably getting a little too invested in this but the polish really shows through as everyone in this game is totally unique, even through most of them are all just different bugs and beetles.
lastly I will just go over some et cetera type things that get me giddy about how much I love this game. There's the ability to cut most background objects, which react based on what theyre made of and everything; it's just a nice touch that makes sure youre never left without something to interact with. Theres the incredibly simplistic depiction of the main character, who is the only one who never speaks and also doesnt have a mouth (I sort of wonder which came first in the design process). There's also the charm system in it's entirety, which lets you sort of develop youre own playstyle with only small, yet impactful differences in how the game works. Each charm also has a very noticable amount of work put into it, and lots of polish. For example, a charm which only costs 1 "notch" (decides how many charms you can equip, better charms cost more notches) serves the purpose of pulling the currency ("geo") towards you rather than having to walk over it. This charm actually makes little fireflies fly from your cloak and go pick them up and bring them to you! It's a very small touch, but the type of thing that I really appreciate in a game.
TL;DR
Pros:
==>Wonderful, immersive soundtrack
==>Lively, animated as hell art
==>huge replayability
(like any metroidvania, you can go wherever whenever, along with the charm system described above)
==>very in depth, yet simple combat that's a blast to master
==>interesting bosses
==>Simple upgrades
(This one is probably a more minority opinion, but I really appreciate that rather than opening a menu and equipping a new item you found and potentially having to swap between them for puzzles, upgrades are things like walljump or dashing, things that are simple on the surface but completely change how you move around and fight enemies without interrupting the flow of gameplay to swap out abilities).
==>PRICE
(10$ on sale during the winter sale????? I wouldve easily payed 60 for this gem had I known how much I'd love it. Not to mention the free DLC that has already come out, and I believe more is coming.)
Cons/Pros/Sorta both:
==>Backtracking with a huge sense of progress - development on this below
(I really couldn't decide where to put this because I usually hate backtracking, but this game is somewhat different. Like any metroidvania/game where most of the map is available to explore from day one, you will have to move through previously discovered rooms quite often. Despite this inherent flaw in a genre, I found myself enjoying it in this game, as there are constantly rooms you passed by before but didn't go into because you were lost, or you were preoccupied with going somewhere else, or you didnt have the upgrade to go there. Youre constantly finding new things in old places, whether that means whole new items/rooms, or simply a new way to move through the room with your new walljump, this game constantly reminds you that you havn't tried everything.)
Cons:
==> I genuinely can't think of any at the moment, if I do this review will be the first to know

Take Starpoint Gemini 2, Freelancer, Elite Dangerous and the worldbuilding of Starcraft 2, throw into a foodblender. Put on high for two minutes.
*WHIRRR*
This is the result. A gorgeous, whisky-soaked blend of a game where pilots drink greel distilled alcohol, where antimatter specks are used for deviant practices, and where combat takes place on a horizontal plane straight out of Assassins' Creed : Black Flag, on crack. All handled with the colour and panache of the original Torchlight, which exploded out of nowhere and revitalised the Dungeon Crawler genre. This promises, and mostly succeeds in doing the same for space exploration.
In the time honoured tradition of all space exploration games everywhere, you are thrown into a starter ship, in this case, a dinky little corvette with a few broadside cannons, a few turrets, and a hull made of papier mache and shields made of soap suds. It is your job to find your Aunt Juno, who so very kindly left you this ship, and find out why you've been dragged out to the tail end of space, which is full of the scum of the universe, and work your way up the foodchain, blowing up said scum and villainy, and eventually become owner of a pimped up ship of doom and destruction. Depending on your playstyle this may be a top notch destroyer, with speed and agility and tons of guns, or a dreadnaught with a horrifying number of broadsides, or a heavy hauler with enough armour to qualify as having it's own gravitational pull.
Or, y'know, you could buy a strike craft and try to outrun bullets, but that's for the clinically insane. Even top level shields and good guns won't allow you to toe it with the enemy dreadnaughts for -long-, but hey, whatever flicks your switch!
Rebel galaxy gives you a very, very diverse set of tools to work with, you can tool up for mining with lasers and fault scanners, or you can go full out commodity trader, and the economy is set up enough to actually handle that, with system averages and station histories that actually work properly and can be scanned from out of station across the system, allowing you to set up profitable trade routes back and forth. This can pay off very nicely once you have a high capacity hauler, particularly if that hauler has one of the contraband cargo expansions which means you can facilitate life as a smuggler on the side.
Or you can just blow things up, because explosions are pretty. Blowing things up always work, and there's a terrifying variety of weapons, not just purchasable, but also lootable unique variants which can be discovered in the world, in loot crates or from the hulls of pirate lords, if you feel like converting them to scrap metal.
Rebel Galaxy offers a -lot- of activities, and offers enough in each activity to have you happily whiling away your time, moreso than Elite Dangerous did (and yes, I know many E;D fans who are going to burn me for that, but it's true), the mining is more sensibly handled due to the tractor beams, the combat is more visceral and less grindy, the trading makes more sense and doesn't require an excel spreadsheet to get the best out of. There's a real economy, and you don't need to be online to get the most out of the game.
There are -two- buts to this rather delicious soup.
One : The factions - They are present, but they're rather bland. More time and depth could have been put into them, faction exclusive ships for each faction would have been glorious, along with modules, as well as faction exclusive bases that you could dock at, along with missions and different reactions based on standing, as well as more complex interrelations between said factions. Right now you basically have only two paths you can follow. If there's anything that could exponentially increase the lifespan of this game - Faction DLC would do it. This would convert a 20-40 hour game to a 200-400 hour game. No joke.
Two : Whilst the activities are good, they all tend to peter out once you get out past the destroyer mark, and the fact you can only hire gunship level mercenaries puts a hard cap on the kind of fights they can throw at you. Hiring capital level mercenaries would have solved this. Again, faction DLC for the win here.
Do these two issues stop this game from being anything other than excellent? No. It's still a bloody great game, and for the price point they're charging it's an absolute steal. It does however prevent me from slamming the "Essential" badge on, because I know that the devs could quite possibly get the Factions some love, and make this "the" game to beat. Hint hint. It does, however, easily merit being a game that people should look into, especially if you're someone who loved Freelancer, or similar games.
Verdict :

Review update:
I actually got a response from customer support, they couldn't recover my cards, but they did credit enough coins to my account to purchase boosters equal to the amount I lost.  Since my negative recommendation was based almost entirely on losing my initial packs, I am for now changing the review for positive.  This doesn't mean that I necessarily "recommend" the game, but I am very pleasantly surprised that my problem was actually addressed by support.
Original Negative Review:
The game started out promising, the mandatory first campaign chapter/tutorial that some people complain about was ok for me even though I already know how to play magic, and I was excited about having a free to play model where you are guaranteed to have a complete collection after a finite amount of grinding (or money spent).  However, I ran into the problem where you are forced to choose cloud or local save because it was out of sync and I lost all my farmed gold and many of the cards from the starting three packs.  (I chose cloud, but I've read online that choosing local will also lose your progress - it's basically a you will lose your cards no matter what message).  This basically put my account in a worse place than a starting account would be!  This is absolutely unacceptable for an online game - that you could lose all your cards at any time.  I sent an email to support to try to get my cards back, but all I got is a stock response.  Normally I'd be grinding the AI now for 15 coins per win until the daily gold cap, but I don't have much motivation to do it if I know I can lose all my progress at any time.  If they fix this problem or refund my cards I'll try this game again - but I'm not very optimistic about either one happening.

Can't believe I never wrote a review for this till now. Split into played original/new sections.
If you played the original Sins of a Solar Empire, this feels like another addon. Buffed graphics, addition of Corvettes (rapid raiders who will tear up frigates and long range frigates) and Titans (yes, basically what that suggests - will take on several capital ships no problem). Couple of new techs based off your Loyal/Rebel alignment, making for somewhat different play styles, especially involving diplomacy. Ever wanted 2 TEC starbases in the same gravity well without mods? Play TEC Loyalists. Wanna stripmine planets into dead asteroids like a proper Vasari? Loyalists. Care to set fire to entire worlds with righteous Advent hate? Loyalists again. Good for immersion. Would not recommend DLCs unless you're feeling rich. 5 bucks is a bit much to pay for a couple of new planet types and the ability to specialize a planet in commerce or industry. Same applies to the Stellar Phenomena DLC. It adds to the immersion and would recommend if they were like $1 each, but 5's a bit much for so little content. Definetly not on the scale of Entrechment/Diplomacy.
New to the series? It's a RTS. Not a micro management game though, in fact the game promotes macro managing - the lower the shields on a ship, the higher the damage mitigation. No mass firepower orders here! Well, capital ships excepted, I prefer to blow those up before letting the AI handle the rest. Typical 4x Space RTS - start with a homeworld, colonize more, build ships, blow up enemies, make friends - and backstab them if you feel like it. Each side is balanced properly with no glaring advantage beyond numbers. That's not to say you can just spam nothing but heavy cruisers; proper fleet composition is key in this game series. Planetary infrastructure is basically just upgrading its capabilities - no GalCiv construction here.
Would I recommend it? Sure, it was a good waste of just under 100 hours while I grabbed all the achivements. Be warned that it's basically nothing but skirmish gameplay - no campaign.

Pro/Con:

Cons:

It's a really fun, fast-paced game. The matches last roughly ~10 minutes, so it's really easy to play one game or a series of games and gauge your time responsibly. It's also got really low requirements, so it can even be run on computers you buy from a computer shop for $249; does not need a lot of power at all.
It feels really balanced, which is really impressive. If you take a look at the "tier" list of champions, there are some champions that are overall 'really good' but there aren't any champions that are 'really bad'. For example, in the C-tier you have Jumong but I've seen Jumongs out-play many a Varesh, who is in the S-tier.
The community is generally pretty good. Sometimes, if you're playing a champion from a 'higher tier', you'll get BMers saying, "Oh, you're just playing a broken champion," or, "X is just the same as Y from LoL." Sorry? I think this is the caustic mentality that comes from Dota2 and LoL, and I don't think it's bad at all in Battlerite. People tend to be pretty courteous: "GG!" or "Nice job!" or "GR (great round)" are very common.

Saints Row: Gat out of Hell is a standalone expansion to Saints Row IV and it stays completelly true to the game controls, fights system, special skills logic system and graohics engine. If you enjoyed Saints Row IV you will also enjoy this short expansion.
I'm writting this strictly under the line set ever since SR3 was out, because that's when the Saints Row franchise jumped completelly out of the GTA like type of story telling and into overdosed craziness and hilariousness.
PROS
✔ Hilarious script writing as always. The game stays true to the new humor stadarts set ever since Saints Row 3 was out and keeps it up to the very weird crazy level that suits.
✔ You get to have parodies, easter eggs and references here as well. The whole game is like a reference to teh Constantine movie and there's some hilarious Disney parody hidden in it, I should let you fidure out the rest.
✔ If you liked SR4 and the special powers concept then you will love this as almost all of the skills you had exist here as well but this time with difference forms/ effects/ visuals and animations (for example you get to fly with wings instead of gliding).

I liked Saints Row 3 and Saints Row 4 quite a bit, especially after playing through the game cooperatively with my boyfriend. After those game, I was on board with more hot SR gameplay! However, Gat out of Hell disappointed me greatly.
Basically, Gat out of Hell consists entirely of those side activities you did for people in SR3/4. While SR4 had side quests done for people to get bonuses but also had unique main quests, this game has you doing ONLY side quests. The only real "unique" quests are when you rescue people who defy Satan, but these are short lived.
You do these in order to♥♥♥♥♥♥off Satan and get his attention, so you can draw him out to kick his♥♥♥♥♥ The progress for this is shown on a meter on the TAB screen, and it fills as you do these quests as well as cause chaos around the town. Once you hit certain milestones, cutscenes play and things change slightly for the overworld. When the meter fills, you unlock the final mission, which is a boss fight against Satan. Beat it, you win the game.
What I just said is hardly a summary. Side activities are ALL you do for the large chunk of this short game. If you've played SR3/4, you will recognize them because they're basically the same save for some slight modifications (Blazin', where you race through arrow checkpoints, now involves flying instead of sprinting).  The only three new side activities involve powering up an altar with one of your superpowers followed by a short hoard-mode sequence, one where you unlock teleport points by activiting statues then defeating a big brute enemy, and one Domination-style one where you must activate three zones to take over a building while preventing enemy minions from taking said zones back from you. These new activities still feel like retreads however, and lack much variety.
Switching gears to talk about some minor issues, there generally feels like a lack of care put into the game. The voice acting lacks any sort of enthusiasm or emotion, and the writing comes off as terse, even forced at times. When doing online coop, sometimes the activities would not activate for my coop buddy and required me to finish them (thankfully he still got the quest completed after I did it).
What made me very sad is that this game just isn't funny, either in its written gags or visual jokes. I can only think of one moment that I found pretty amusing, but the rest of the game only has a few visual jokes (such as billboard ads or business name branding) and, as I mentioned before, poor writing and VA execution results in a lack of charm I've come to expect from the Saints Row games.
The streets of Hell do not excite in the least. The starting industrial area feels drab and lacking in life, and only really matters since that is where you start when you reload your save. The most interesting area has to be the market/amusement park/red light district New Hades, but even then it feels empty with little to do or see.
Lastly, and perhaps the thing that made me the saddest, must be the complete lack of customization! Gone are the various clothing stores, the taunts/complements, or even interesting vehicles to drive (save for a monster truck police vehicle). The only store provided consists of a vending machine that lets you buy ammo, upgrade weapons, and pay to get the Hell-cops off your back. It feels so impersonal and, adding with what I said about the writing, sucks a lot of charm that this series has.
I really am disappointed. I feel like this game was made on a budget, which its default price reflects. However, I'd argue that the good kind of budget games are those that put a lot of polish, charm, and love into a small experience rather than a large, average but bland one. Unfortunately this game is the latter. If you've played SR3 and/or SR4, just avoid this game. If you haven't, go play both those games because they're fun, especially with a buddy to tag along!

Just got through the campaign in nine hours - and that's WITH revisiting some areas to finish a couple of side quests.  That being said, that's how much time you're going to spend on a single play-through.  If you're going to do a run with all three characters, and on both normal and heroic difficulties, you're looking at 50 to 60 hours of semi-original gameplay.  Coop is something I'd like to do sometime.  Maybe that'll add another 20 hours.
Have you guys ever played Lord of the Rings: Third Age?  This feels like that game if it were shorter and didn't have turn-based combat.
Really quickly, I'm going to give a run-down of what I definitely do and do not like - spoilers ahead.
I liked the world: The devs of this game did an absolutely outstanding job of creating their world, however stunted it may be in certain areas.  Rivendell and Nordinbad were good examples due to how outstanding the architecture was, but the best area for me was the Barrow-downs.  They NAILED the atmosphere for that area, and looking out at all the outstanding crags and jagged rocks planted in the rolling green hills gave me chills.  Inside Gundabad was epic as well, being able to look across the void and see all these different things going on.
I like the weapon system: There are a bunch of weapons in the game: hand-axes, battleaxes, short swords, long swords, hammers, staffs.  You can dual-wield one-handed weapons after unlocking a specific perk thing.  While I've only played as the Ranger, there was still a great deal that I could toy with.  It seems to be about finding your style, but there's also moving between dual-wielding and broadsword wielding in order to balance damage and speed.  Also, weapons break down after time and need to be repaired by a forger.
Similarly, I like the equipment system:  Giving yourself the best armor while looking for repairs on what's about to break.
I like how weapons and equipments can be imbued with properties: You know, stuff like ice damage, fire damage, shock damage.  Boosts to strength, stamina, health, power.  Same kind of gimmick from Skyrim, but executed well here.  Some equipment/weapons do not have slots - others have multiple.   Fun figuring out what to trade off - damage or health?
I like the checkpoints: almost every level will have checkpoints where you can sell your loot, buy very basic things like weak armor and potions, and you can return to the last safe area (Bree, Rivendell, Nordinbad).  Good for getting out if you need and dumping inventory.
I'm conflicted on the lore.  I like what it tries to do, especially regarding fallen Dunedain cities and Carn Dum and the dwarves, but it comes off as something that these three characters should not be able to rise up against.  Aragorn wants you to defeat Sauron's right hand man, like no big deal champ thanks for the help?  Oh wow check out these sick dwarves taking out the whole of Mt. Gundabad with this awesome secret weapon?  That's literally Deus ex Machina.
I'm conflicted on the combat.  It's monotonous, but the perk(???) system makes it a bit interesting.  Once again, that's not something I've fully explored, but it breaks the monotony of LMB spam and the RMB coup-de-grace.
The only real hate I have is for a Mannish faction that follows Agandaur.  The grunts of this Mannish faction are overpowered.  Their swords extend beyond what their model shows, and they attack FAST.  They do not get knocked back.  Don't expect an easy one-up over these guys.  Spam your special attacks and ranged.  Or the devs can fix these guys, whatever.
Can't think of anything else that I really do hate.  As a Tolkien fan who wanted more but knew this wasn't canon at all, I give this a 7/10 because I got it on sale.  Do not get this at full price.

The Stanley Parable is a game that's fun, endearing and worth playing, but it is nothing more than that. If you are looking for a different experience to what is offered in the gaming industry currently then play this. If you are looking for a self-aware break down of the gaming industry through clever rhetoric and 3rd wall breaking, then the game does 3/4 of those things. The message is nothing new, and the execution in places is slightly sloppy. Whilst this could be argued to be intentional, I would argue that it hampers the experience slightly too much for my own liking. If you're willing to suffer through several quality of life improvements remaining noticably missing then you'll plough through the game's multiple branching paths with glee. If you demand tighter, more accessable ways to access such content yourself without grinding through the same story - with minor fluctuations - to find the larger more noticable differences, then this game is not for you.
Short, concise and to the point, the Stanley Parable is worth the money in a sale, but don't expect anything ground-shattering.

The first 30 minutes to an hour of the game is awesome. The fact that the narrator actually interacts with his story and that you, as the player, can break that story (It's a spoiler, but I knew that before going into the game and it didn't take away from the experience) is really unique in a game, and The Stanley Parable pulls it off wonderfully.
However, as time goes on and you get used to the narrator, the game loses a lot of its charm. That's why, I think, the developers made many endings so bizzare, like you jumping from game to game, entering unfinished rooms, getting into "button heaven", or the confusion ending. It makes up for the narration, but doesn't last more than 3-4 hours before it too gets boring.
After a couple hours, the intentions of the player shift from wanting to "see what's over there, and oh, what's this here, and I wonder what happens if I..." to focusing on getting all the endings. There are plenty, but I feel like this mentality takes away from the game, and the fact that it involves a fair bit of repetitiveness (you'll have to hear many voicelines good 5-20 times) doesn't help.
Basically, it's a great and unique game, but it's entertaining only for 3 hours. Thus, I don't feel like it's worth the 12 dollars I spent on it. So why do I recommend it? Because sales are a thing

I don't play many platformers or Metroidvanias in general, and I certainly don't go for games that require one to "git gud." Somehow though, this sucked me in from the very first minute. The art style and soundtrack are incredible. Sometimes it's creepy, sometimes it's a little silly, sometimes it can be heartwarming, and sometimes it's just intense. The level design is solid, with a lot of branching paths opening up after a short while to encourage exploration. The game is pretty challenging (in my opinion anyway), but never feels insurmountable in difficulty. Even if a boss is problematic, there's a pretty good chance it can be skipped and fought later with some more upgrades. Everything builds up at a good pace, layering new skills on top of old ones to really give a sense of progression from having a merely sword and a jump at the beginning to having a whole arsenal of spells, dashes, improved health, etc. by the end game.
There are a couple minor flaws that I found. I wasn't crazy about how the map worked, requiring a charm slot (basically a passive upgrade) in order to track your location at any time. There's also a very challenging platforming section towards the end (not required to complete the game, but required for 100%) that feels a bit out of place and tests a lot of platforming skills that weren't really required for anything else. Veteran platformer gamers seem to have less trouble with it, but someone like me who enjoyed the gradual difficulty scaling might find it frustrating and off-putting. The story is pretty vague as well, but there are interesting lore bits that can be pieced together or people far more dedicated than I am on YouTube to shed light on it. That's obviously not a flaw so much as an artistic choice, but it might be a con for people who like strong narratives.
I'd give it 9.5/10. You can't beat the price, at $15 (or $10 on sale), the 40-50 hour experience for a first run is excellent value.

Okay, so I'm sure most of you know how I (and most of the Internet) feel about the first BioShock, but hardly anyone I know has played the sequel. I'm gonna be honest and straightforward with you: it isn't as good as the first. However, I still think it's better than Infinite.
The combat system has been much improved from the first game, especially the plasmids. The endings are more varied and interesting, and less cookie-cutter than the "hurr durr ur evil u bomb da world; ur good u raise da gurlz to happy grownups" of the original. The main drawbacks to the game are its shorter length, simpler story, less interesting villains and side characters, ADAM harvesting system designed purely to make the game seem longer, and the thoroughly usless multiplayer that's more empty than your wallet after a Steam sale.
Even with all of these issues, however, I still consider it a worthy installation in the franchise. Would I pay a full $20? Probably not, but then again I'm the kind of guy who doesn't buy a game unless it's 75% off, no matter how good. But if it's one of those $5 specials, and if you consider yourself a fan of BioShock, then there's no reason not to pick this one up.

Having played and enjoyed the original version for like 1000 hours, Rebellion did not dissappoint, adding fancy tech like an extra starbase per gravity well (TEC loyalist) or moving them to other ones fully upgraded (Vasari Rebel, yeah, I like starbases, what can I say?) along with Titans to lead your ships into victory (they really help with breaking down fortifications).
To those new to the game, Sins of a Solar Empire is a space based strategy game that is quite easy to get into after following the tutorials, it basically revolves around colonizing planets (nothing fancy, you just change its ownership and upgrade it for increased tax income or building more space structures around it), building ships/defenses, de-colonizing hostile planets! I never experimented with mods and mostly emphasized single player, but here is my views on this game from that perspective:
pros:
- easy to learn resource system that is used for everything, forcing you to focus resources on one aspect (economy/research/fleet/defensive structures) at a time.
- best logistics system I have ever seen for a game, you basically pay upkeep for increasing your population max which cannot be reversed, strongly mitigating rush tactics.
- awesome effects and graphics if your comp can handle it, will slow down the game if it has trouble, leading to disconnects in multiplayer.
- capital ships can earn experience and level up to gain new skills (different for each kind of capital ship, 6 capital ships per faction) while raising their stats.
- full camera control, allowing you to view at nearly any angle or scale.
- high replayability, there are many options to change, many ai/map/team configurations for a lot of fun.
neutral:
- games can take 6-12 hours without quick start, I like that, but it is something to keep in mind.
- pirates are very hard to deal with for beginners, but you can just turn them off. Me? I enjoy the extra capital ship experience ;)
cons:
- your main view (where you can observe one full gravity well) contains mostly just basic icons, not the awesome graphics screenshots like to show off.
- higher ai levels gain huge bonusses to resource gains, I wish there were an ai with all the smarts but none of the cheats, since even hard ai does not properly upgrade starbases (to mitigate Novalith Cannons for instance, unfair does).
- the diplomacy is kind of lame in my opinion. I mostly play with locked teams since diplomacy requires both sides to like the other. Sounds obvious, but it is very hard to get yourself to like other ai players, which is required for a cease fire (from there, things get easy with envoys).
- all frigates/cruisers from all factions barely differ from one another except for just one truly unique support cruiser.
- no story/campaign.
Overall I would give this game a 9.5/10 with pros easily outweighing the cons.
As for dlcs: I truly recommend the forbidden worlds for both increasing the variety of colonizable planets as well as adding a planet specialization option.

I see a lot of negative reviews for this game. But for a free to play experience that I sunk nearly 50 hours (20hrs of which was spent completing an arduous but, for accessibility's sake, necessary campaign / tutorial) I can say that the game works well for all levels of magic players.
I have played duels of the planeswalker games previously and felt like they were a vapid waste of time. The Devs here instead of releasing a new planeswalker game every year are going to be ADDING NEW SETS OF CARDS as they are released in the Magic universe. This is why it is a better investment of time than previous games because it removes the limits of sets available at the given time per game release.
As a casual Magic player I enjoy not having to spend actual money to gain cards if I chose the grind. The grind is part of what makes the game fun too. The lower tier in the leaderboard season is good because you don't generally feel outmatched. Once you get up to rank 10+ I find you see some more serious decks/players.
I agree with some of the negative feedback such as not having a chat feature. Perhaps implementing a system similar to hearthstone where you only have a set amount of gestures/commands would do?
Some reviews said the AI was too difficult the AI I find is no less skilled than a human player who knows how to play magic properly. They do some silly things like play a combat bonus into play creatures after attacking etc. If you know how to make a decent fast deck then you will just have to make your starting draws count by exploiting the restart duel function and voila... you win vs. AI.
The weekly/daily quest system is OK... I can usually grind out 1-2 boosters per day if I'm playing casually and WINNING lots.
**Note** If you lose a match you get no Coins at all. This makes losing frustrating although you can leave any time and you will be replaced by an AI instead of a forfeit out right ending the game. I feel this limits your ability to grind quickly via forfeits. I can see the balance in this.
All said and done, I will continue to play Magic Duels. I may even spend money some day as the game grows.

So to start off with some of the things I loved:
Flight- Oh my gosh yes, this was one of the things I was excited about as soon as I saw the trailer, everything from the detail of the wings (the mechanics are smooth as butter) to the fact that it makes exploring far more dynamic, more than just running or jumping up the side of a building.  In fact flight abilities were one of the first things I focused on upgrading, I genuinely enjoy flying around the map.
Powers- This ties in with the flight aspect but quite honestly I loved having all sorts of powers that I could just quick tap to swap to and use, this means that after a while fighting baddies became well childs play.  If my aura didn't stun them or my stomp didn't crush them my little minions were on the case, the only power I found I rarely used was blast but that was because I already had decent weapons and felt the other 3 powers were OP enough to handle whatever came my way.
Story- Now this one could be debatable, some people felt the story was too short, I honestly enjoyed it, I was super surprised that such a simple plot could be so much fun to play.  Despite how short it was I felt compelled by it, it was simple, clean, and yet it still manages to draw you in.
However with every good tale there are bound to be things that were quirky or just unlikable in general, I found while I truly enjoyed playing the game that there were still things that left me wanting... It's not that they were detrimental to my enjoyment of the game but they did stand out enough for me to list them.
Poor controller support- Yep, this could have been a deal breaker for me, could have except that when I switched to the keyboard for the first time I found that the controlls were really well laid out.  Ok so I really got bummed out that the flight mechanic was horrid with a 360 controller and it nearly made me stop playing, but then I read that other people had a similar controller issue and learned to live with it, I simply adapted to the keyboard and went on to finish the game.
Too much power- Yeah, it's ironic one of the things I loved about the game is also something I am not as fond of.  I am a collector so to give you an idea I had collected a ton of the 'souls' and upgraded my powers (to my level max) before I had all of my abilities, therefore I was going into early level missions like gaining support from allies with a lot more strength than usually seen.  I was also able to upgrade some powers immediately after gaining them which meant that I could do loyalty quests (missions set by your allies) with ease, for most of the loyalty missions I would leave with nothing less than a gold which takes me to another point
Quests are too easy- Yep, even the 'hard' level missions on the map were a piece of cake with the right strategy (ie cycle powers, use guns, repeat) after a while I found myself bored by the idea of 'another' high flying adventure that was far too easy to get a gold in.
Quests are repititious- This sort of ties in with the other points, everything on the map in order to get 100% takeover (an achievement earned by completing everything in each district and the final boss) is just repeating over and over, some map sections had multiple districts with the same quest in it, there was nothing new just a change of scenery.
Story wasn't affected by your pace- This might take a bit to explain but without too much detail your are trying to make a certain character mad, you have a meter on your menu that fills up with the activities you do, when you hit certain 'points' on that meter you get a cut scene which shows game progression.  However after that cut scene ends that's it, it's pretty jarring how quickly you will fly through the checkpoints of the game and reach the final boss point by completing activities.  In fact I managed to hit a checkpoint that involves the kidnapping of your allies before I had even finished recruiting them... It was really odd trying to figure out how to save someone I hadn't even met yet, there was just no sense of urgency to recruit my allies first and even after I had done it there was then no urgency to rescue them, no timing, no anything.
Overall you have to give the game props for what it did right, it was a solid stand alone DLC that introduced a pretty cool set of mechanics to the Saints Row universe (or rather built upon the ones of Saints Row IV) and was pretty fun to play.  Therefore I would definitely say it's worth giving it a try, however I would definitely wait for a good sale price as the current price tag is perhaps a bit much.

What can I say?  This game rocks!  Great FPS!  Story is great!  Characters are interesting!  If you're into the whole WW2 era, like I am, then you will absolutely love this game!  I highly recommend playing this game first, if you're thinking about getting into the Wolfenstein series!  And for you retro gamers out there, try Wolfenstein 3d!  Another great classic!

*Choices at the start of the game - (e.g. +2 food, production ect in each city) with "quests" giving optional bonuses for different buildings (e.g. an extra point of culture for monuments or no maintenence cost for them) allowing greater specialisation. you are never limited by the fact there is only 8 factions. Unlike civ 5 where some factions were especially powerful perhaps even inbalanced.
*Ideologies - The three main ideologies are all realistic, compelling and ultimately lead to different styles of play and win conditions. Solving one of my main gripes with CIv 5 in that your civ almost always favoured a victory so doing your best to win involved simply repeating a tried and tested strategy.
*Tech web - While confusing at first glance and for a couple of playthroughs time it really does allow you to specialise. In civ 5 that one player with the highest science got first dibs on every wonder, not anymore!
*Aliens replace barbarians - More than just a cosmetic change the aliens are not inherently hostile and will treat you differently based on how you treat them. Some are hilariously overpowered at the start of the game but can be avoided. The difficulty setting probably has an effect too.
*Orbital layer - Allows another layer of military conquest where you can rain death from above with massive units or orbital weapons. But also satilites that can create new resources on blank tiles allowing you to develop the map in very new ways. I would love to see this be pushed further to allow a more earthlike climate for the purity ideology.
*The game is outright missing some of the features that came with DLC for civ 5 and will probably end up being DLC later down the line. Including: religion, natural wonders, world congress, tourism/culture victory.
*The game does not have distinct phases like Civ 5 which were based on different eras of human civilisation. As such it the game doesnt really have the same flow of technological advancement making it hard to see how well you are doing in comparison to your rivals. In times of peace this can make the game feel extremely detached almost like no progress is being made at all, at least in war you can see new units duking it out!
*Unlike barbarians the aliens do not not gain any new units over the course of a game. Making them very strong to begin with but the weaker ones quickly become little more than wasted movement points as your units effortlessly plough through them.
*Very little interaction with AI players - The only new addition being that the AI will compliment you if you same the same attitude towards the Aliens or for choosing the same ideology. Civ 5 was lacking in this regard as well, it simply isnt interesting to deal with them in any way.
*Visuals while functional arent exactly amazing. Beyond earth being a stand alone game rather than a paid DLC for Civ 5 means there was an opportunity to up the visuals, which was clearly missed as the game looks to be on the same level of graphical fidelity as civ 5.
tl:dr
Different enough from Civ 5 to be worth trying (I have enjoyed it thus far), similar enough to make you realise whats missing or hasnt been improved.

Not as great since Gamespy closed it's servers, but this game at one time was the ultimate multiplayer FPS if you overlooked the overpowered VTOL and a few bugs most of these problems could be solved by server's modding the content for balance.. There is a website look for for crysis1 online that allows you to modify your game so you could play online still.. plus its a very small 10mb download.
However as you might expect most of the servers were almost dead... not like launch with 10+ 32 player servers packed full.. but on the weekends you might even get a full 32 player game!
As far as the SP campaign goes it's a toss up to me their were a few good parts but a lot of it was really repetitive, here's a bunch of Koreans in a jungle go kill them then repeat.. for half of these areas I just used super speed and cloak and just went straight to the checkpoint lol. Had a lot more fun in the sandbox editor or playing other players SP mods I'd rate the Crysis SP campaign as 5/10.
Back to multiplayer in my opinion it still has the best multiplayer elements ever done. Super speed, strength and the seldom used but still great cloak. Then there's the double jump glitch which actually was great and didn't unbalance anything but allowed you to scale to the top of buildings but still took a touch of skill (you don't make the jump and you could fall and die) and you couldn't just double jump anywhere you had to be next to a vertical wall.
To give you a first person experience of what awesome things you could do, you could hear a tank rolling in and buy C4 near the Mctiller's prototype weapons facility area thats littered with a few industrial buildings and a giant pipeline. Jump to the roof and go prone- wait for the right moment and super speed jump off the 10 ft roof throw both C4's onto the tank, proceed to land while the tank tries to turn his turrent around but he's too slow-press trigger and bam you usually got a kill or at least a severely damaged tank.
For helicopters you got a laser guided LAW missle, you could fire all 3 rockets with your laser pointing straight up, javelin style and then hold your sights directly on the middle of the rotor. One missle there and it was instant explosion but it wasn't too uncommon for you to be only a 100 yards away and the helicopter would instantly target you- your only hope if the heli started unloading missles directly at you was to wait until the last second and strength jump and switch back to regular armor mode- while you prayed you could keep your sights on the heli and that your missle would hurry up and hit him- Usually at the last second KABOOM heli explodes and you land with like 5 health or die from his last missle impact!
If a enemy car was headed straight for you and you were feeling brave instead of just jumping over it like most sane people do you could go into strength mode and if you timed it perfectly- punch the front of the car's grille and it'd pop the back end off the ground, destroy the motor and instantly stop the vehicle and from there if you were fast enough you could bring out your weapon and just shoot down the still seated shocked pidgeon(s). Most of the time though if you tried this and the player lagged or you just didnt time it exactly right ( the cars can go 60 mph) you'd just get ran over lol.
One of my personal favorites was the lack of knifes in favor of punches, you'd go into super speed mode and close in on someone real quick and switch to strength mode and one punch and he'd be insta dead flying through the air till he hit a wall- this was a lot harder than it sounds though as you were more vulnerable and one shotgun blast to the torso and you were down.
The American base on the MESA map which was huge probably one of the largest 32 player maps ever created at that point in time was perfectly created- so many differant roads and bridges and hills, which led up or down ( the base was situated about 400 yards back from a massive dam which if things got real you could drive off of and then bail and land in the water and try and swim deep to avoid getting picked off by base♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥heli's.. There were just so many well placed options that unless your team really really sucked you could definetely break free of any strong hold on your base and take a spawn bunker.
However the Koreans had a big disadvantage on the map being on ground level and having the fastest route being a tunnel to go through to reach the center point of the game the Mctiller's prototype facility... Needless to say one enemy tank at the end of a tunnel is never a good thing. But as long as team's were balanced it didn't really matter literally one really good player could swing the entire game sometimes and that's really saying something because the sheer amount of options and tactics+skills that could be used was incredible, you could really respect or hate a good player.
Honestly if they'd of ironed out the Vtol or just never had the bloody VTOL in the first place kept the AAA gun effective and not OVERLY powerful and added some leveling system or custom skins ect to keep players enticed to keep playing.. It'd of really hit it out of the ballpark.. but there just were some annoying bugs too many hackers and the most annoying bunker♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥undestroyable VTROLLS that really hurt this game.
I vote Crysis online to be Remastered for 4k rebalanced 64+ player servers and a new SP campaign. Although it'll never happen... I just wish I could go back and play it on the best servers with my updated hardware lol my GTS 8800 never exceeded 30 fps and was more like 15 half the time on low.

Even when this game is often cataloged as a melee "copy" this game is very unique in every possible way.
First, the characters, when did smash had a character that could burn you and make dps? When did smash had a character that could freeze the stage and then freeze you entirely?
Those are just two examples of a very unique game, every movement of every character is very unique, there aren't two same-different versions of the same move, for example, Marth's and Roy's up air, and just because these unique characters you should give it a try.
Next, the unique options, first of all, the shield doesn't exists here, instead there is a parry, think of it as a counter that lasts few frames but if the opponents hits you while you are parrying the opponent gets stunned.
Then the ledges, they don't exist here, you have to go directly to the stage, this is the fun part and how you manage to recover.
There are a lot of other things that are very unique but instead of listing them all here, why don't try the game and discover them for yourself? If you like smash in general you should give this a try, it's fun, people always says "don't trust to strangers" but trust me, you won't get bored.
TLDR; Very fun, unique smash-like game that won't get you bored

This game is pretty much PC Melee with easier tech, but that doesn't mean it's a cheap clone. In fact, there are many things that set this game apart.
For example:
- No shielding, instead you parry, which almost is like more forgiving perfect shielding
- No ledges, instead you wall jump to reset your recovery
- Airdodging out of specials
- Unique character mechanics, such as Orcane's traps or Etalus' ice
- Constant balance updates that make every character more or less viable at the highest level of play
- Great netplay
This game is an easy recommendation to Melee players/fans and casual gamers looking to get into a Smash-esque game as it is very easy to pick up but very hard to master.

Foreword: I played this game much more on the 360 before I finally made the jump to the PC master race, I only bought it on here to play with my friend. Although I thought I'd like to share
It's good, certainly not great. It has as much replay value as Champions of Norath did (if you ever played it), in that you can replay the game i NG+ on harder difficulty. The combat is mostly mindless, but it's the larger enemies that make it fun, especially the trolls. Learning when to roll between their legs and when to strike takes a bit of time but you get down soon enough. The character progression is neat and clean, nothing special. It does however offer some breathing room with characters, basing your dwarf entirely on crossbows rather than the standard berserker 2-handed cookie-cutter dwarf is a lot of fun. In fact, the dwarven crossbow and the explosive bolt skill is the most powerfull attack in the game (as far as I've seen).
The Ranger is about as bland as you'd expect, and the Elven mage only has 1 game-breaking skill that the AI is surprisingly competent with. The elven mage lays down a giant bubble that blocks all projectiles coming in. It can be upgraded to heal allies inside, amplify the power of friendly projectiles going out, and an explosion when the timer goes out that knocks nearby enemies away. This is best left to the AI to control (or a friend if you play 3 players) to use, while you play one of the other two, more competent, characters. The elven mage does have the bonus of infinite ammo (it does deplete and have to recharge though).

This War Of Mine reminds me that danger lurks from every corner. It is not only the lack of food and medicine that could end your life, but there's always the constant threat of bandits who will take everything you've worked for away from you. And how did I work for my supplies? By murdering innocent people. I thought the threat was over when I stole food from an elderly couple, but the aftermath of that decision caused the character who commited the murders to leave, while the other survivors were depressed about the loss of one of their own.
I don't know what caused the world to go to sh*t, but I do know that there are multiple threats to be aware of. Depression. Hunger. Violence. I didn't even survive long enough to experience the threat of (possible) betrayal. This is a truly accurate war simulator. I don't know if I /want/ to call it a game because I often associate that with having fun and with This War Of Mine, you won't have fun.
But this is an experience I'd definitely recommend, if you're up for it. Those who are susceptible to various triggers such as suicide might want to stay away from it.

Play this game, but approach it with caution.
It's a neat take on platformers- you cut your own platforms out of the world around you. You can cut, push, and pull your way through the world. I see some players had a lot of issues with this game, which I didn't... not until, of course, the very end of the game, when it became the most frustrating.
If you're familiar with platformers and puzzles, you can glance around you and see what you have to do. There's secret casettes to find, and you can change the song playing, which is neat. There's a few boss encounters as well. Everything went over for me without a hitch, until the very end, when suddenly there was a lot of lag and glitching.
Because you cut your own levels, sometimes you can get stuck somewhere in the worst way possible, and you will seriously have to kill yourself by cutting a slice of rock and pulling it down onto your own head so you can start over. You can also cut so many pieces that the game doesn't seem to know what to do with its own physics anymore.
Other than that, I really did love the art, the characters, the music, and the feel of the game. It was silly and serious at the same time. It was a fresh perspective on platformers. It was fun to build my way to get to the secret rooms.
Oh, and the radio you carry has an attitude.

I bought this game in the recent sale and wow... just wow. This game is incredible on all fronts and is quickly becoming one of my favourite games. If you like the souls games, this is definitely one for you, and I don't mean that in a memey "hurr hurr its hard so its like dark souls", there are so many more similarities than just that in terms of the protagonist, the themes and the execution of this game. A quick rundown.
Pros
+ Large open world with lots of hidden secrets
+ A great level of diifculty where deaths rarely feel unfair. Learning an enemies/bosses attack pattern and using this to kill them is INCREDIBLY satisfying.
+ Epic soundtrack
+ Gorgeous artstyle
+ Great lore and large parts of it are up to you to find.
+ Enthralling story
+ Very little handholding- the game throws you in and expects you to find your own way pretty much. If you want, you can pretty much avoid most upgrades/charms and do the bare minimum to finish the game, or you can really take your time to learn everything go your own way.
+ Amazing price for what you get, I'd gladly pay £60 for this game
+ ALL DLC IS FREE
Cons
- If you don't like backtracking, this might get annoying. There is a lot of it but imo it feels good because you come back to areas with new upgrades and find secrets
- My reactions are pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥♥so some of the bosses got annoying for me (but never enough to make me want to quit the game). This isn't really a con as much as it is my experience with the game.
Conclusion: Hollow knight is a masterpiece, as close to a 10/10 game as you can get. For how much you pay for this game, there is no reason you shouldn't get it and support the devs.

Full review:

First of all, the game is very short, especially if you don't replay it to get the huge amount of available achievements for fun. If you are the kind of human who complains about games being short, make sure you are getting this in a sale.
That said, I had a lot of fun with this game. The graphics style is unique and interesting, the dialogue is witty and charming, but the strongest point of the game are the tools that are at the games core. This is a first game that I am aware of, that gives you a tool to cut up 3d blocks in realtime. You can also interact with most of the environment and basically destroy most of the level that way.
Cut up, pull or push blocks as you are trying to cross over multiple beautiful levels in this game while following a quite silly story of the game. You are on a quest of retrieving the pants that your grandfather left you as a heritage. Sadly your big brother stole them and run off to some desert.
Look, the game is weird, but that's what's great about it. I totally recommend it for a short fun experience. I hope the developers do more with the technology they have at their hands.

The mechanics are well defined. Controls feel tight and responsive. Follows the ideology of Metroid where you gather abilities which unlocks new ways of approacing the world, and therefore unlock new areas organically. Combat is also very responsive and every fight feels fair.
It is very atmospheric. Biomes like forest sound like forest; valleys sound like valleys which howl. Overall, excellent ambiance, but same cannot be said for OST.
On the surface, the story feels as intricate and deep as the Dark Souls, but it is not even close. It certainly does the job by adding a overtone which adds to the atmosphere, but it could have been better.
It is amazing. Everything is (even the levels) inspired by bugs. It finds a really good ground between cutsy and grim. One of the best.
The game is difficult at first, but as soon as collect abilities, the difficulty drops. Having said that, the bosses feel difficult and satisfying.
We are stuck with the same weapon and armor (technically, there is no armor). I would love to see some new weapons and "hats" in future mega update.
The world is intricate and interwoven. Hollow Knight promotes exploration when you enter a new biome. You can later find a map-maker who gives a map (for money, ofc). World is huge, and Team Cherry can add new areas as DLCs to expand it even further.

Not as great since Gamespy closed it's servers, but this game at one time was the ultimate multiplayer FPS if you overlooked the overpowered VTOL and a few bugs most of these problems could be solved by server's modding the content for balance.. There is a website look for for crysis1 online that allows you to modify your game so you could play online still.. plus its a very small 10mb download.
However as you might expect most of the servers were almost dead... not like launch with 10+ 32 player servers packed full.. but on the weekends you might even get a full 32 player game!
As far as the SP campaign goes it's a toss up to me their were a few good parts but a lot of it was really repetitive, here's a bunch of Koreans in a jungle go kill them then repeat.. for half of these areas I just used super speed and cloak and just went straight to the checkpoint lol. Had a lot more fun in the sandbox editor or playing other players SP mods I'd rate the Crysis SP campaign as 5/10.
Back to multiplayer in my opinion it still has the best multiplayer elements ever done. Super speed, strength and the seldom used but still great cloak. Then there's the double jump glitch which actually was great and didn't unbalance anything but allowed you to scale to the top of buildings but still took a touch of skill (you don't make the jump and you could fall and die) and you couldn't just double jump anywhere you had to be next to a vertical wall.
To give you a first person experience of what awesome things you could do, you could hear a tank rolling in and buy C4 near the Mctiller's prototype weapons facility area thats littered with a few industrial buildings and a giant pipeline. Jump to the roof and go prone- wait for the right moment and super speed jump off the 10 ft roof throw both C4's onto the tank, proceed to land while the tank tries to turn his turrent around but he's too slow-press trigger and bam you usually got a kill or at least a severely damaged tank.
For helicopters you got a laser guided LAW missle, you could fire all 3 rockets with your laser pointing straight up, javelin style and then hold your sights directly on the middle of the rotor. One missle there and it was instant explosion but it wasn't too uncommon for you to be only a 100 yards away and the helicopter would instantly target you- your only hope if the heli started unloading missles directly at you was to wait until the last second and strength jump and switch back to regular armor mode- while you prayed you could keep your sights on the heli and that your missle would hurry up and hit him- Usually at the last second KABOOM heli explodes and you land with like 5 health or die from his last missle impact!
If a enemy car was headed straight for you and you were feeling brave instead of just jumping over it like most sane people do you could go into strength mode and if you timed it perfectly- punch the front of the car's grille and it'd pop the back end off the ground, destroy the motor and instantly stop the vehicle and from there if you were fast enough you could bring out your weapon and just shoot down the still seated shocked pidgeon(s). Most of the time though if you tried this and the player lagged or you just didnt time it exactly right ( the cars can go 60 mph) you'd just get ran over lol.
One of my personal favorites was the lack of knifes in favor of punches, you'd go into super speed mode and close in on someone real quick and switch to strength mode and one punch and he'd be insta dead flying through the air till he hit a wall- this was a lot harder than it sounds though as you were more vulnerable and one shotgun blast to the torso and you were down.
The American base on the MESA map which was huge probably one of the largest 32 player maps ever created at that point in time was perfectly created- so many differant roads and bridges and hills, which led up or down ( the base was situated about 400 yards back from a massive dam which if things got real you could drive off of and then bail and land in the water and try and swim deep to avoid getting picked off by base♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥heli's.. There were just so many well placed options that unless your team really really sucked you could definetely break free of any strong hold on your base and take a spawn bunker.
However the Koreans had a big disadvantage on the map being on ground level and having the fastest route being a tunnel to go through to reach the center point of the game the Mctiller's prototype facility... Needless to say one enemy tank at the end of a tunnel is never a good thing. But as long as team's were balanced it didn't really matter literally one really good player could swing the entire game sometimes and that's really saying something because the sheer amount of options and tactics+skills that could be used was incredible, you could really respect or hate a good player.
Honestly if they'd of ironed out the Vtol or just never had the bloody VTOL in the first place kept the AAA gun effective and not OVERLY powerful and added some leveling system or custom skins ect to keep players enticed to keep playing.. It'd of really hit it out of the ballpark.. but there just were some annoying bugs too many hackers and the most annoying bunker♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥undestroyable VTROLLS that really hurt this game.
I vote Crysis online to be Remastered for 4k rebalanced 64+ player servers and a new SP campaign. Although it'll never happen... I just wish I could go back and play it on the best servers with my updated hardware lol my GTS 8800 never exceeded 30 fps and was more like 15 half the time on low.

This game is great! You'll be able to find a lot of reviews listing its general qualities, so I'll just talk about my experiences with its combat.
Note: This is not a 3D movement dogfight space combat sim,  combat in this game is closer to what you might find in old naval battles
Combat against a mixed enemy fleet is truly a multitasking excercise. You'll be using your boosters to keep yourself alongside larger enemy ships so you can use your broadside cannons, timing your deflector shield uses to block their incoming broadsides/missles, and spamming X button to fire EMP flak at the smaller ships so you can focus on the big target.
I find myself having to think about positioning alot, and having to boost away from larger ships or swarms of small craft while i swing my own ship around because the big hole in my leftside hull cant take it anymore, so i reorient and come in from a new angle.
So far about 50% of my combat has been outside of mission running. You'll often find distress beacons, get tips from bartenders on bounty locations, or just plain run smack into an enemy fleet while warping somewhere else.
Certain missions seem really unbalanced at first, but after refitting to the right weapons or adopting new tactics, suddenly theyre totally manageable.
It is generaly to easy, but fun. Enjoy it.

Crysis is a 1st person shooter masterpiece.  You wear a nanosuite that grants you either armor, speed, strength or stealth.
The good:
1. The game looks amazing.  Yes, the game is ten years old, but it was THE performance benchmark for many years.
2. The music is fantastic.  The game has full orchestra music that blends in seamlessly with the game.
3. The game puts a lot of emphasis on stealth.  Even with your suit's powers you die easily if you confront a bunch of enemies heads-on.  You could sneak into the perfect position by using your stealth abailty, but you need to be patient.  You could go in guns blazing, but you would need to be smart about about it; use cover and move quickly between positions.
4. The enemies' AI is pretty good.  They will hide, ambush or swarm you if you are not careful.
The bad:
5. My pc crashed a few times from over heating because of playing this game.  I maxed out all settings.
6. The nanosuite is nothing a cool as shown on the intro movie.  You cannot string-up spectacular moves in quick succession.  Your energy runs out too quickly.
7. Your enemies can tell where you atack from, even when you perform a meale attack or use a silenced gun.  I think this game needed a way for you to kill enemies soundlessly at close quarters.  But then again, I love stealth games.
The ugly:
Nothing

This review is mostly for Magic Newcomers i guess, because anyone who likes MTG already needs to try this Game without discussion.
Its the best Digital Magic the Gathering TCG released so far, and there is still much potential left to grow and get even better. I played for about 10 hours now to finish the Campaign and play a few Duells vs AI, and i had fun.
The freetoplay Model is fair, much more then Hearthstone is.
Boosters are 150 Gold and you earn 15Gold per win vs AI and 30 Gold per win vs Players.
In Hearthstone its 100 Gold per Booster and 10 Gold every 3 Wins!
The Quests you get every Day to earn extra Gold are pretty much the same.
The UI is well done in my opinion, including much help for new Players and faster Gameplay for advanced ones.
The graphics and effects are fine and do thier Job, i like how it looks.
There is a detailed Tutorial for everyone new to Magic, its very well done and easy to understand.
I can only recomend this Game, its new so there are only 250 Cards in yet, but the next Addon is already in progress.
So everyone whos intrested, just Check it out. Its for Free after all...
UPDATE:
After a few hundred hours of playing and deck building and 3 expansions later, i still recomend it.
Even more now because of all the new Cards added.
It still has its edges and there will be a lot to do until its finally polished, new cards mean new bugs, while older buggy cards gets fixed in the same time.
But the most important thing is that it is fun to play, gather new cards, build new decks and try out new combos or invent complete new ones.
It is 100% Magic the Gathering.

I haven't had any problem with the PC version and it's everything you can expect if you happen to like Saints Row 4. For newcombers to the series, it's a $20 standalone title that is a mini-version of Saint's Row 4. If you haven't played Saints Row before, it's an open world crime sandbox game similar to Grand Theift Auto. However, most have said it has veered away from the crime element and it has really jumped the boat when it comes to the story and the humor. If your looking for a serious crime GTA style game, then I wouldn't recommend it. But, for those that like superpowers, fun weapons and romping around doing activities, it's a solid title.
A few of the problems I have with this is the activities seem way too easy to complete. Often times, you exceed the goals with time to spare. There are some missing features, such as character customization and radio stations and the short length, but that is attributed by being a cheaper standalone version of Saints Row. The last problem is if $20 is worth it for a cut down version of Saints Row, however...I did pick this up on sale for $10.
I would recommend it if you like open-world games with a good sense of humor. The theme of hell helps out and if you don't want to commit to Saints Row 4, then this is a cheaper alternative as a look to where the series is going.

What an amazing game.
The player conducts a small group of civilians in a war, and the objective is to survive and to remain human. Of course, surviving sometimes is at odds with retaining one's humanity, and that is precisely where this game comes alive. From looking into abandoned places to getting into direct confrontation with other people in the war-torn city we live in, the player is faced not with the adrenaline that is usual in war games, kill baby kill style, but with those emotions which actually can be associated to what war-survivors tell when they write their memoirs: fear, compassion, uncertainty, so much uncertainty, hope, and above all, despite for war and those who pursue it.
Everyone who ever played a war videogame from the pov of the soldier should play this game. Hell, this game could very well be the basis for a whole new industry that does not only require students to read die welle (germany) or lord of the flies (USA), but indeed requires them to play games in order to look at things in new ways, and truly without much effort. This is an amazing piece of art. The only way in which the word "entertaining" is applicable is if taken in the same sense clockwork orange, or the pianist, are "entertaining movies". Most of all, they are captivating experiences.
Perhaps the best game of the year, despite (or perhaps precisely because of) coming from such a small studio, and capable of making a lot of people take videogames more seriously.
